examBlueprint.tests: B5.1: the chloroplast with both stages placed, the light reactions, or the Calvin cycle
Interpreting scientific text; passage drawn from B5.3 (the light-reaction passage)

standards.title: Overview of photosynthesis and the chloroplast
standards.titleAsPrinted: Overview of Photosynthesis and the Chloroplast
standards.description: Students explain what photosynthesis does and where it happens.
iCan: I can write and explain the overall equation: carbon dioxide plus water plus light energy yields glucose (sugar) plus oxygen
I can explain that photosynthesis is redox that stores energy: CO2 is reduced to sugar and water is oxidized, the reverse electron direction from respiration
I can label chloroplast structure: the thylakoids (stacked into grana), the thylakoid space, and the stroma
I can name the two stages and where each happens: the light reactions in the thylakoid membranes, the Calvin cycle in the stroma

exam.examItems: MC Q1, Q2, Q8; SA 11, 12; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: Capturing light: pigments and the spectrum
standards.titleAsPrinted: Capturing Light: Pigments and the Spectrum
standards.description: Students explain how pigments capture light energy.
iCan: I can describe visible light as part of the electromagnetic spectrum, with different wavelengths seen as different colors
I can explain that a pigment absorbs some wavelengths and reflects others, and that the reflected light is the color we see (leaves look green because chlorophyll reflects green)
I can identify chlorophyll a as the main pigment, and chlorophyll b and the carotenoids as accessory pigments that broaden the light captured
I can explain that pigments are organized into photosystems that funnel absorbed light energy to a reaction center

standards.title: The light reactions
standards.description: Students explain how the light reactions turn light into chemical energy.
iCan: I can explain that light excites electrons in photosystem II, and that water is split (photolysis) to replace them, releasing O2
I can trace the energized electrons from photosystem II down an electron transport chain to photosystem I, then to NADP+, forming NADPH
I can explain that the electron transport pumps H+ into the thylakoid space, and chemiosmosis through ATP synthase makes ATP
I can state the products of the light reactions (ATP, NADPH, and O2), and that the O2 you breathe comes from split water

standards.title: The Calvin cycle
standards.description: Students explain how the Calvin cycle builds sugar from CO2.
iCan: I can state that the Calvin cycle runs in the stroma and uses the ATP and NADPH from the light reactions (it needs no light itself)
I can explain carbon fixation: the enzyme rubisco attaches CO2 to RuBP
I can explain reduction: ATP and NADPH convert the fixed carbon into G3P, a sugar
I can explain regeneration: most G3P rebuilds RuBP so the cycle continues, and that it takes three CO2 to make one net G3P (two G3P make one glucose)

exam.examItems: MC Q6, Q7; SA 16; Part 3 CER

standards.title: C4 and CAM photosynthesis
standards.description: Students explain adaptations that protect photosynthesis in hot, dry climates.
iCan: I can explain photorespiration: when it is hot and dry, stomata close, O2 builds up, and rubisco fixes O2 instead of CO2, wasting energy and making no sugar
I can explain that C4 plants (corn, sugarcane) separate carbon fixation in space, fixing CO2 into a four-carbon molecule in one cell and running the Calvin cycle in another
I can explain that CAM plants (cacti, succulents) separate it in time, fixing carbon at night and running the Calvin cycle by day with stomata closed
I can connect both strategies to conserving water while still feeding the Calvin cycle CO2
